scenes.title: 그림에서 게임 리소스로
lines: Imagine putting this character into a game. A nice standing image is not enough if the bag changes sides or the face changes during motion. We will follow the process of preserving the design, matching pixels and backgrounds, and preparing animations and effects.

scenes.title: 생성·정리·검수
lines: It helps to separate generation, processing, and validation. Image models propose artwork. Processing tools normalize size, color, and transparency. The engine reveals how the assets work at their actual display size. The eight public tools serve different steps; you do not need all of them at once.

scenes.title: Character Design (캐릭터 디자인)
lines: Start by fixing the character design. List the hairstyle, clothing colors, accessories, and bag position that must remain unchanged. Our reference uses a yellow hair clip, a teal jacket, and a brown bag. Whether using NovelAI or another image tool, select one design before collecting more variations.

scenes.title: Turnaround Sheet (방향별 설정화)
lines: A turnaround sheet shows the front, side, and back of one character. A reference image can guide an image generator to preserve clothing and proportions while changing the view. Still inspect the sheet: compare the hair clip, the strap across the back, the shoes, and the sleeves.

scenes.title: Dataset (학습 데이터)
lines: If you need repeated poses, use the sheet as the standard for your training set. Front views alone do not teach the side or back. Combine varied NovelAI poses with ChatGPT turnaround views, correcting or excluding inconsistent details. Twenty to fifty curated images can be an experimental starting point, but coverage and accuracy matter more than a fixed count.

scenes.title: LoRA (저랭크 적응)
lines: LoRA is not the image folder itself. It is an adapter that learns a low-rank weight update instead of retraining the entire base model. It adds learned character or style information to the model's existing capabilities. Images and captions are training inputs; the LoRA file is a learned result.

scenes.title: Style + Character (스타일과 캐릭터)
lines: Pixel style and character identity have different roles. A style LoRA shapes how an image looks, while a character LoRA helps specify who appears. Tools such as kohya_ss and OneTrainer must be configured for the base model you intend to use. Adapters from unrelated model families are not freely interchangeable.

scenes.title: ComfyUI (노드 기반 생성)
lines: In ComfyUI, start with a checkpoint: the base image model. Load an Illustrious XL model and a compatible pixel-style LoRA. If you have trained a character LoRA, chain another LoRA node after it. Connect both MODEL and CLIP so the appropriate model and text-encoding changes reach the rest of the graph.

scenes.title: 같은 조건에서 강도 비교
lines: Hold the prompt, resolution, and seed constant when comparing LoRA strengths. The seed controls the starting randomness. A weak style influence may look more like an illustration; too much may damage small details. Change one strength at a time and inspect the features that need to survive. A fixed seed does not lock the pose or accessories, so inspect those changes too.

scenes.title: 생성에서 저장까지
lines: The graph continues beyond the model and adapters. Text is encoded, a sampler denoises the latent, and the VAE decoder turns it into visible pixels. Resizing and saving follow. Keeping these stages separate lets you retain an image while comparing reduction methods and palettes. Add a character adapter once its trained file is available.

scenes.title: Pixel Grid (픽셀 격자)
lines: An image that looks pixelated is not automatically a usable pixel-art asset. Zoom in and the apparent blocks may be uneven or blurred. Pixel art needs a consistent logical pixel grid. Decide the asset's native game resolution, then normalize the generated image to that grid.

PixelArt SakuLike ILXL is described as producing pixels enlarged roughly eightfold. For that setup, 768 by 1344 can be reduced to 96 by 168. The point is matching the generated structure to the game's logical grid, not memorizing a universal reduction factor. Other models and images may need a different scale.

scenes.title: Palette Quantization (색상 수 제한)
lines: Next, inspect the palette: the set of colors used by the asset. Too many near-identical shades can add noise. Quantizing each frame independently can cause flickering. Use a consistent character palette and check whether key details remain legible. Fewer colors are useful when they clarify the form.

scenes.title: Alpha + Retouch (투명도와 리터칭)
lines: A checkerboard painted into an image is different from real transparency in its alpha channel. Place the sprite over light and dark backgrounds to reveal fringes and leftover colors. Clean edges and stray pixels in an editor such as Aseprite, then inspect the native game size as well as the zoomed image.

scenes.title: Outpainting (배경 확장)
lines: Independently generated characters and backgrounds can disagree in color and object scale. One approach is outpainting a scene that already contains the character, extending its surroundings while retaining visual context. Remove the character from the background layer so a separate sprite can occupy that space.

scenes.title: 배경과 캐릭터의 기준 맞추기
lines: After expansion, compare pixel scale again. A one-pixel character outline can clash with much chunkier furniture edges. Choose a reduction scale from the actual grid, then match character and object proportions. Repair broken boundaries such as floor seams and chair legs rather than regenerating the whole scene unnecessarily.

scenes.title: 정지 이미지와 연속 동작
lines: These steps already support still assets for dialogue games and visual novels. Walking and attacking introduce temporal requirements: consistent identity, grounded feet, stable scale, and connected starts and endings. The eight tools address different parts of this remaining work.

scenes.title: 01 · 2dimg2motion
lines: 2dimg2motion organizes key-pose redraws and in-between frames from a character reference. Establish anticipation, the main action, and recovery first. Its default pattern uses fourteen frames, but a frame count alone does not guarantee good motion. Inspect identity, limbs, baseline, and scale before packaging transparent frames and a sheet.

scenes.title: 02 · sprite-gen
lines: sprite-gen supports image-based rows and video-derived loops. It connects generation with keying, frame extraction, loop selection, and atlas packaging. An atlas combines images on a texture with their locations recorded as metadata. Distinguish the generation provider from the tools that process its output.

scenes.title: 03 · pixelfx
lines: pixelfx is useful for flames, explosions, and sword trails. Code draws the pixels over time instead of asking an image model for every new frame. Keep the motion while changing a palette, then run the effect directly or export transparent frames for playback in a game engine.

scenes.title: 04 · PixelOE
lines: PixelOE helps with cleanup by reinforcing important outlines before reduction and palette processing. Pixel Snapper is another option for regularizing messy pixel structure and colors. Neither should be confused with motion generation. Compare their actual results, especially thin lines and facial features.

scenes.title: 05 · Agent Sprite Forge
lines: Agent Sprite Forge packages a master image into multiple actions through per-action video generation, keying, registration, loop selection, and timing. It also includes map and tile workflows. Review transitions between actions: a convincing run still fails if its scale or foot baseline jumps when switching from idle.

scenes.title: 06 · Codixel
lines: Codixel emphasizes references, code, and skeletal motion. A long tail or body can be organized around linked control points. Reusing image parts allows localized motion changes, but it does not invent unseen surfaces during a turn. Those need additional artwork or another generation step.

scenes.title: 07 · Pixelbolt
lines: Pixelbolt describes colors, shapes, and frames in editable JSON recipes. These spirit variants were rendered from the same recipe with a changed palette, not redrawn by an image model. Similar targeted edits can change an eye or a frame. This suits small sprites, icons, and repeatable effects.

scenes.title: 08 · Sprite Sheet Diffusion
lines: Sprite Sheet Diffusion is a generative research approach conditioned on a reference character and a sequence of poses. Local inference requires compatible model weights and software, not just source code. Inspect the generated frames for clothing, face, and motion consistency; it is not simply a one-click editor.

scenes.title: 내게 필요한 경로 선택
lines: Choose a route from the asset you need. Still characters and backgrounds emphasize design and pixel cleanup. Motion requires a choice among key-pose generation, video extraction, and rigging. Code-based methods work well for effects and small assets with precise edits. One model does not have to handle every step.

scenes.title: Unity Import (유니티 적용)
lines: Import the PNG as a sprite and use Point filtering when you want sharp pixel boundaries. Slice a sheet into frame regions in the correct order. Pixels Per Unit controls the asset's scale in world units; the pivot defines its placement and rotation reference. Keep these conventions consistent across a character's actions.

scenes.title: 게임 안에서 확인할 것
lines: Validation goes beyond opening a file. Check edges on light and dark backgrounds, and proportions beside scenery. Play motion at normal speed, then step through frames to inspect sliding feet, scale changes, and loop seams. Check game timing too: an attractive generated video may still respond poorly as an action.

scenes.title: 무료 코드와 생성 비용
lines: Free code does not mean free generation services. A tool's MIT or Apache license does not replace provider terms or the conditions for the base model, adapter, training images, and output. It also does not clear rights in someone else's character. Record versions, sources, and required notices with the project.

scenes.title: 게임에 맞게 완성하기
lines: The core is consistent design, normalized pixel and asset conventions, and validation in the actual game context. AI can generate candidates and assist repetitive work. Turning those candidates into usable assets depends on the decisions and checks that follow generation.
